overview: Two-arm cluster randomised trial: 36 of 38 inpatient wards randomised 1:1 to the tiered or standard drug interaction alert display for six months, stratified by hospital and ward specialty.
population: Adult inpatient wards in the three hospitals, excluding the two intensive care units, which use a separate alert configuration; all high-severity interaction alerts raised on participating wards.
exposure: Tiered display: high-severity interactions interrupt the prescriber with a modal alert; moderate and minor interactions appear as a passive note in the order summary. Potassium-raising combinations stay interruptive in both arms for patients with reduced kidney function.
procedures: The vendor enables the display per ward after randomisation by the trial statistician. Each month, a random sample of high-severity alerts per ward is reviewed by two pharmacists blind to arm where possible, using a written definition of an appropriate response. Pharmacists run targeted surveillance of dispensed moderate combinations from a short list of high-risk pairs in both arms. Prescriber rotation is recorded from the rota system.

outcomes.name: Appropriate response to high-severity alerts
outcomes.measure: Proportion of sampled high-severity alerts accepted or overridden with an appropriate reason, judged by two pharmacists
outcomes.why: Captures whether prescribers act on the alerts that matter, not just how often they click.

outcomes.name: Harm from moderate interactions
outcomes.measure: Dispensed high-risk moderate combinations judged by pharmacists to have caused or contributed to harm, per 1,000 patient days

outcomes.name: Exposure to the other arm
outcomes.measure: Proportion of orders written by prescribers who also worked on wards in the other arm that week

feasibility: Double review of about 20 high-severity alerts per ward per month (720 alerts at about four minutes each) takes about 48 hours a month for each of the two reviewers, roughly 0.6 FTE in total, which fits within the 2.0 FTE team only if targeted surveillance is limited to the short list of high-risk pairs.
biasMitigation: Pharmacist reviewers blind to arm where the alert history allows
Written appropriateness definition fixed before review
Recorded prescriber rotation for a contamination sensitivity analysis

biasFlags.label: Contamination through rotating prescribers
biasFlags.note: Expected under 10 percent with ward randomisation; measured directly.

biasFlags.label: Reviewer unblinding
biasFlags.note: Alert display type may be visible in the record.

parsimony.simplestPath: Two arms, one primary outcome on a pharmacist-reviewed sample, one harm safeguard.

theoreticalFramework: None beyond the trial design; alert fatigue is treated as a volume-attention problem.
summary: Ward-randomised trial of 36 wards with an appropriateness primary outcome and harm surveillance.
